title: Salle Pleyel concert and the unclear percentage contract
summary: Canetti booked the Harlemites at the Salle Pleyel to good reviews and more recordings, but made the musicians sign contracts on an undefined percentage basis.

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: All right, now, we've just been sorting ourselves out as to how we're going to proceed at this point. But we're going to go ahead, now, really, with Mr. Briggs talking about the Harlemites and his playing career in Paris, running after this band got started. Now, Canetti was managing for you, he was booking the band and managing

Yes, uh-huh. He was the booking agent of the band, and he booked us at the Salle de Pleyel concert, which was -- came over nicely. We had nice write-ups and everything else, and the orchestra was fine. It seems like we had a pretty nice following, not only of musicians, we had a pretty nice following of patrons, you know, people who were interested in what we were doing. And then --
Well, the Salle de Pleyel concert was kind of a break for you --
Oh yes, yes. 'Cause we made the other recordings after. We made the other recordings after the Salle de
We made the other recordings after the Salle de Pleyel. Then, Panassie -- Canetti, started booking the orchestra.
But the point is, you see, he had us all sign a contract on a parietal basis, but on the parietal basis, we didn't know what his parietal was, you see.
Parietal means that you can't -- with a big orchestra, you can't -- you must have a certain sum, and then divide into parietal --
But he just wanted us to sign, well, you get the 10/15th or or 10/20th or something, you know -- and he didn't know.
